generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No canonical parcel relation, legal boundary, connectivity score or utility connection is inferred.

extra_examples.site: England and Wales registered freehold land
extra_examples.fact: HMLR INSPIRE polygons show indicative position/extent and link through an INSPIRE ID, but they are not exact legal title boundaries.
extra_examples.gate: Title register/plan or equivalent exact legal evidence remains required.

extra_examples.fact: Current INSPIRE polygon files were published 5 July 2026 and are refreshed monthly.
extra_examples.gate: Freshness does not remove the indicative-boundary caveat.

extra_examples.ref: Local land charge migration gap control
extra_examples.site: England and Wales local land charges
extra_examples.fact: HMLR states not every local authority has migrated local land charge data to the service yet.
extra_examples.gate: Absence in the dataset cannot be treated as absence of a local land charge.

extra_examples.fact: HMLR reports more than 25 million titles and 28 million polygons in the National Polygon Service.
extra_examples.gate: Coverage scale does not prove exact legal geometry for a specific title.

extra_examples.fact: HMLR says an index polygon may be the same size, larger or smaller than the extent shown on the title plan.
extra_examples.gate: Do not use index polygon geometry as an exact parcel boundary without legal/title-plan verification.

extra_examples.fact: HMLR's restrictive-covenant dataset identifies titles with a covenant but does not provide the covenant terms.
extra_examples.gate: The underlying register or retained document must be read to assess development impact.

extra_examples.fact: HMLR notes leases granted for more than seven years generally must be registered, while some shorter leases are also registered.
extra_examples.gate: Registered lease presence does not establish project land control or vacant possession.

extra_examples.fact: HMLR documents possible typographic and matching errors in company registration numbers and proprietorship fields.
extra_examples.gate: Company-number and proprietor matches require independent verification.

extra_examples.ref: Price Paid Data current-month revision gate
extra_examples.fact: HMLR advises that the May 2026 current-month release should not be used in isolation because later registrations add to the dataset.
extra_examples.gate: Treat current-month transaction counts/prices as incomplete and revisable.

extra_examples.site: Great Britain public transport access nodes
extra_examples.fact: Planning Data reports current NaPTAN coverage but labels the dataset-level platform origin MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
extra_examples.gate: Prefer DfT-authoritative entity records and route/service evidence for exact analysis.

extra_examples.fact: An authoritative station node supplies a precise point and NaPTAN metadata but not walking route, service frequency, capacity or travel-time score.
extra_examples.gate: Exact parcel accessibility must be calculated rather than inferred from a point.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data's local-plan dataset is labelled MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement even though it indexes current, emerging and historic plans.
extra_examples.gate: Use the planning authority's live adopted/emerging plan for parcel policy assignment.

extra_examples.fact: The Planning Data mineral-safeguarding-area dataset currently contains zero records and has not attempted collection.
extra_examples.gate: Zero records must never be interpreted as zero mineral safeguarding constraints.

extra_examples.fact: Official planning guidance says only a specific investigation can establish whether contamination is present.
extra_examples.gate: No contamination score may be created from historical land-use suspicion alone.

extra_examples.fact: Before granting outline permission, an authority should understand contaminated conditions sufficiently to be confident remediation is viable and practicable.
extra_examples.gate: Outline status does not waive contamination evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Planning guidance allows plans/applications to require land- or slope-stability risk assessment where landslide, mining or subsidence issues are relevant.
extra_examples.gate: Exact geotechnical/mining evidence is required for a parcel.

extra_examples.fact: Official guidance says good acoustic design should be considered early where development creates noise or is sensitive to the acoustic environment.
extra_examples.gate: No universal fixed threshold can be applied without site/proposal assessment.

extra_examples.fact: Transport Assessments/Statements can establish whether residual transport impacts are likely to be severe, which may be relevant to refusal under national policy.
extra_examples.gate: Severity must be established from proposal-specific network evidence.

extra_examples.fact: 2026 Local Transport Plan guidance says authorities should routinely use the government's Connectivity Tool to identify well-connected locations and intervention opportunities.
extra_examples.gate: The exact site score/scenario still has to be run before Future Growth scoring.

extra_examples.fact: RIS3 commits £27 billion across the strategic road network for 2026-2031.
extra_examples.gate: National investment cannot be assigned to a specific development unless a named scheme and site relationship are verified.

extra_examples.fact: DfT Connectivity Tool produces a national connectivity measure for a selected location and can test route interventions.
extra_examples.gate: A score must be generated for the exact canonical location; nearby station points are insufficient.

extra_examples.fact: Ofgem's June 2026 decision allows phased Gate 2 offers through 2026 with final batch expected by mid-March 2027.
extra_examples.gate: The programme timetable does not establish any individual project's offer or energisation date.
